newsitem.title: PERU: U.S. ambassador questions Peru warplane purchase.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ambassador questions Peru warplane purchase.

text.p: The U.S. Ambassador to Peru, Dennis Jett, on Tuesday questioned Lima's purchase of Russian-made MiG-29 warplanes, saying the money could be better spent elsewhere.

"It is worth having a debate on what are the priorities of this country and what are its threats," the ambassador told reporters. "For $110 million you can buy a MiG-29 or construct 400 rural schools."
President Alberto Fujimori confirmed last November the purchase of a fleet of MiG-29s which he said would replace an ageing airforce. But he did not give details of numbers or cost.
Military sources, however, said 12 planes were bought, while opposition legislators said Congress had approved in secret $350 million for the transaction.
Fujimori described the purchase as "a sacrifice" and argued that the transaction was economically favourable for Peru.
Jett warned, however, that "the purchase of weapons has the effect (of) producing a reaction in other countries ... that seek arguments to buy weapons. This could now lead to an arms race."

Neighbouring Ecuador, which fought a brief border war with Peru in 1995, is also believed to have purchased four Israeli fighter planes late last year. The two countries began in Brasilia earlier on Tuesday a third round of peace-talks, aimed at permanently solving their long-running border dispute.

Jett has irked the Peruvian government in recent weeks by voicing his opinion on various internal matters including the dismissal of judges from the highest constitutional court, the torture of an intelligence agent and freedom of media.
"I agree with some of the complaints of the Peruvians and of those who govern them," he said. "However, I will continue to express the opinion of my government."
